papers.title: Mapping Bone Marrow Cell Response from Senile Female Rats on Ca-P-Doped Titanium Coating.
papers.abstract: Chemical and topographical surface modifications on dental implants aim to increase the bone surface contact area of the implant and improve osseointegration. This study analyzed the cellular response of undifferentiated mesenchymal stem cells (MSC), derived from senile rats' femoral bone marrow, when cultured on a bioactive coating (by plasma electrolytic oxidation, PEO, with Ca2+ and P5+ ions), a sandblasting followed by acid-etching (SLA) surface, and a machined surface (MSU). A total of 102 Ti-6Al-4V discs were divided into three groups (n = 34). The surface chemistry was analyzed by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS). Cell viability assay, gene expression of osteoblastic markers, and mineralized matrix formation were investigated. The cell growth and viability results were higher for PEO vs. MSU surface (p = 0.001). An increase in cell proliferation from 3 to 7 days (p < 0.05) and from 7 to 10 days (p < 0.05) was noted for PEO and SLA surfaces. Gene expression for OSX, ALP, BSP, and OPN showed a statistical significance (p = 0.001) among groups. In addition, the PEO surface showed a higher mineralized matrix bone formation (p = 0.003). In conclusion, MSC from senile female rats cultured on SLA and PEO surfaces showed similar cellular responses and should be considered for future clinical investigations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究牙科植入物表面涂层对老年大鼠骨髓细胞的影响，未涉及用户关注的LPBF制造、应力屏蔽或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve LPBF fabrication, porous structure design, stress shielding, or mechanical testing; it focuses on cellular response to surface coatings without any biomechanical or structural analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究老年雌性大鼠骨髓细胞对Ca-P掺杂钛涂层的响应。
summary_zh.method: 通过等离子体电解氧化制备涂层，与SLA和机加工表面对比。
summary_zh.result: PEO表面促进细胞增殖和成骨分化，矿化基质形成增加。
summary_zh.validation: 细胞活力、基因表达和矿化基质形成分析。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the cellular response of senile rat mesenchymal stem cells on Ca-P-doped titanium coatings for improved osseointegration.
summary_en.method: Plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) was used to create bioactive coatings, compared with sandblasted/acid-etched (SLA) and machined surfaces.
summary_en.result: PEO surfaces enhanced cell proliferation, osteogenic gene expression, and mineralized matrix formation compared to machined surfaces.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture assays including viability, gene expression, and mineralization.
